result.text: The paper tackles instability in Transformer training caused by attention layers becoming pathologically sharp—an effect they call "attention entropy collapse" where heads focus too narrowly, leading to oscillation or divergence during training. The key insight is that low attention entropy correlates with instability and that constraining the spectral norms of linear layers controls the scale of attention logits, yielding a provable lower bound on attention entropy (which decays exponentially with the logits’ spectral norm). The authors propose σReparam, a lightweight reparameterization that applies spectral normalization to all linear layers plus a learned scalar to restore representational scale, and demonstrate across vision, language, speech, and self-supervised tasks that this fix prevents entropy collapse, stabilizes training without warmup or adaptive optimizers, and enables deeper or simpler training recipes to reach competitive performance.

result.text: The paper addresses temporal grounding—localizing a video segment that matches a natural language query—by reframing it as a metric-learning problem rather than relying on complex detection/regression heads or fusion schemes. Its key insight is that richer negative samples, constructed via mutual matching of cross-modal pairs and mined across different videos, strengthen joint embedding learning by forcing the model to better discriminate semantically similar and dissimilar query–moment pairs and thus maximize cross-modal mutual information. The authors propose the Mutual Matching Network (MMN), which embeds queries and candidate moments into a shared space and trains with mutual cross-modal negative pairs and inter-video negatives to directly model similarity, and they demonstrate competitive or superior performance on four benchmarks and a challenge-winning result, validating metric learning as an effective approach for temporal grounding.

The paper addresses the computational bottleneck of Diffusion Transformer (DiT) models, whose self-attention layers incur quadratic cost and slow high-resolution image and video generation. The key insight is that DiT inference exhibits three kinds of redundancy—spatial (many heads attend locally), temporal (neighboring timesteps produce similar attention outputs), and conditional (conditional and unconditional passes are similar)—which can be exploited post-training to avoid repeated costly attention computations. The method, DiTFastAttn, implements three complementary compression techniques: Window Attention with Residual Sharing to localize and reuse spatial attention computation, Attention Sharing across Timesteps to reuse attention maps between nearby diffusion steps, and Attention Sharing across Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) to skip redundant conditional/unconditional attention work; applied to DiT, PixArt-Sigma, and OpenSora, this yields up to 76% reduction in attention FLOPs and up to 1.8× end-to-end speedup for high-resolution generation.

result.text: We propose Decoding-Invariant Refusal (DIR), a test-time guardrail that neutralizes jailbreaks exploiting decoding hyperparameters by enforcing safety/refusal consistency across a randomized ensemble of decoding policies and seeds. DIR performs short-prefix probes under a bank of sampling regimes (e.g., temperature, top-k/p, beams) and a repeat/regenerate step to stay in the model’s natural generation channel, then estimates a binomial lower bound on the refusal (or safety) rate; it flags the prompt or escalates alignment if any unsafe variant appears or the certified refusal probability falls below a threshold. This randomized-smoothing view makes attacks that rely on dialing decoding settings ineffective and pairs naturally with loss-landscape probes as an auxiliary signal. We will evaluate DIR against decoding-exploitation attacks, TAP-generated prompts, and output-filter-evading settings from JAMBench, targeting low added latency via short-prefix probes and caching.

args.text: Ask-or-Move: a mixed-initiative 3D language grounding agent that jointly plans next-best-views and minimal clarifying questions to optimally collapse referential uncertainty. Hypotheses are object-identifier tokens with a factorized belief over attributes and pairwise relations; the agent estimates expected information gain from a camera pose via projected, view-consistent attention fields and from a candidate question via an LLM that simulates how answers partition the hypothesis set. result.text: Transformation-Invariant Refusal (TIR) is a lightweight, model-agnostic guardrail that tests whether a candidate response remains safe across a bank of semantics-preserving obfuscation/normalization transforms tuned to known jailbreak channels. Building on the repeat-to-detect insight, TIR applies repeat/regenerate checks not only to the raw output but also to variants produced by unicode/homoglyph normalization, paraphrase and back-translation, and cipher-decoding via shadow decoders that target ciphered or non-standard character encodings seen in cipher-based and guardrail-evading attacks. The defense flags an answer if any transformed variant (or its repeat) reveals harmful content or if refusals are non-invariant across variants, catching output-filter evasions and token-level triggers that elude single-view detectors. We hypothesize substantially lower false negatives on guardrail-triggering and token-trigger benchmarks at modest query cost, without white-box access or fine-tuning.

result.text: The paper addresses safe reinforcement learning in safety-critical settings by tackling the problem of learning to both satisfy unknown safety constraints and maximize cumulative reward in constrained Markov decision processes. The key insight is to decouple safety learning from reward optimization: first conservatively expand and certify a safe region through exploration under uncertainty, then optimize policy only within that certified safe region to avoid constraint violations. The proposed SNO-MDP algorithm implements this two-stage approach using a stepwise safe-region expansion procedure followed by reward optimization confined to the learned safe set, and the authors prove guarantees that safety constraints are satisfied during learning and that the obtained reward is near-optimal under regularity assumptions. Empirical results on a new GP-SAFETY-GYM benchmark and a Mars surface exploration simulation demonstrate the method’s practical effectiveness.

args.text: We propose Depth-Scheduled Energy-Entropy Attention (DEEA), which treats each attention head as a Hopfield update and imposes a per-layer target entropy profile that decays with depth to mirror the shift from global averaging to metastable attractors. Concretely, we enforce these targets by constraining the spectral norms of Q/K/V projections with a σReparam-style reparameterization to bound attention logits and by adding an energy-margin loss that separates late-layer attractors, making attention an explicit max-margin selector. We further introduce a head-diversity repulsion between attractor basins to promote specialization across heads and scalable memorization. DEEA aims to stabilize training without warmup, mitigate over-smoothing, and enhance in-context learning and recall on long-context tasks.

We propose Discover-and-Enforce PSM Invariance from Passive Video: first learn a video world model and a counterfactual intent/value estimator from action-free data, then automatically discover image-space nuisance transformations that preserve policy similarity, and finally train a representation to be explicitly invariant to them. Concretely, we approximate PSM/bisim distances from passive sequences via intent-conditioned TD and bisimulation-style rollouts, and perform a bilevel search over a parametric family of transformations (e.g., backgrounds, color/style, viewpoint) to find perturbations that minimally change these behavioral distances. We then pretrain the encoder with a contrastive RL objective whose inner products implement goal-conditioned values, augmented with an invariance regularizer applied to the discovered nuisances and a constraint to preserve PSM geometry. This should yield control-sufficient, distraction-robust features that transfer across embodiments and improve sample efficiency and zero-shot generalization on long-horizon, pixel-based control tasks.

We propose Open-Set Calibrated Triaging (OSCT) for domain-adaptive/source-free object detection, which estimates a per-box knownness by fusing category-dictionary reconstruction residuals with a probabilistic teacher’s predictive uncertainty and calibrates it via a task-aware calibrator adapted on target using split-conformal risk control. High-knownness boxes drive self-training; medium-knownness regions trigger localized adversarial/feature alignment; and low-knownness (likely-novel) boxes are masked from pseudo-labels and used only to train an abstention head and to support masked alignment, preventing negative transfer from unknown classes. The calibrator follows a TCD-style auxiliary calibration at source and is bootstrapped on target from teacher–student agreement, while residual cues provide class-conditional pseudo-IoU to disentangle mislocalized known objects from truly novel ones. result.text: The paper tackles safe reinforcement learning in episodic constrained Markov decision processes (CMDPs) where both rewards/utilities and transitions can change over time, subject to known cumulative variation budgets, which complicates combining safe exploration, constraint satisfaction, and adaptation to non-stationarity. Its key insight is that by imposing one of two alternative, verifiable conditions on the time-varying constraints, one can design a primal–dual learning procedure that provably balances dynamic regret and long-term constraint violation even as the environment shifts. The authors introduce PROPD-PPO (Periodically Restarted Optimistic Primal–Dual Proximal Policy Optimization), which periodically restarts optimism-augmented primal–dual updates with proximal policy optimization to adapt to changing dynamics and constraints, and they prove dynamic regret and constraint-violation bounds in both linear kernel function approximation and tabular CMDP settings under the two conditions. This yields the first provably efficient algorithm for safe exploration in non-stationary CMDPs.

args.text: We propose Constrained Energy Flow Attention (CEFA), which computes attention by minimizing a Hopfield-style energy over keys and values subject to flow-conservation constraints and an explicit entropy barrier. In the dual, CEFA becomes a convex program whose solution yields a linear-time attention rule akin to flow-based attention, while spectral normalization of logits enforces a temperature floor that provably prevents entropy collapse and stabilizes training. This energy–flow view induces a block low-rank prior on token–feature structure, explaining emergent token clustering and improving robustness to over-smoothing. We hypothesize CEFA yields more reliable in-context learning by aligning the model’s forward pass with a stable, constrained gradient-flow dynamic that resists mode collapse on long sequences.

Methodologically, they introduce a Probabilistic Teacher framework that estimates uncertainty from a slowly-updated teacher to guide a student via consistency losses, augment localization adaptation with anchor adaptation, and propose an Entropy Focal Loss to weight training by uncertainty; this combination yields substantial gains and new state-of-the-art results.

result.text: Affordance-Guided Compositional Diffusion Planning: train a return-conditioned diffusion model over trajectories and guide its sampling with an affordance embedding formed by stacked value functions of a library of low-level skills. At inference, augment the diffusion score with gradients of a compositional objective built from Boolean algebra over base-task value functions (conjunction/disjunction/negation), enabling zero-shot composition and robust long-horizon planning. Learn the diffusion model on offline data while separately fitting the skill value predictors, and optionally self-evolve by generating reward-guided synthetic trajectories to cover rare compositions. We hypothesize substantial gains on long-horizon robotic and navigation tasks, with ablations isolating affordance guidance vs. Boolean composition benefits.

result.text: The paper addresses improving prompt learning for large vision-language models (e.g., CLIP) by overcoming the limitation of single learned prompts and the collapse that occurs when multiple prompts are naively matched to the same visual feature. The key insight is to represent images and categories as sets of visual and textual features and to use optimal transport to flexibly match multiple learned prompts to diverse visual cues, preventing prompts from collapsing to a single point. Methodologically, the authors learn multiple prompts via a two-stage optimization: an inner loop computes an optimal transport alignment between visual features and prompts using the Sinkhorn algorithm, and an outer loop updates the prompt parameters to minimize this transport-based distance on supervised few-shot recognition data; experiments show consistent improvements over baselines.

result.text: We propose PSM-from-Video Hierarchical Pretraining: learn a policy-similarity–aligned latent space from action-free videos, then use it for hierarchical goal-conditioned control. We first pretrain a latent world model on raw video and derive a policy-similarity proxy by aligning distributions over predicted futures (successor-like rollouts), yielding a representation that approximates PSM/bisimulation without rewards or actions. Clustering this space produces subgoal landmarks; a high-level policy selects latent subgoals while a low-level controller is trained via a contrastive RL objective where inner products implement goal-conditioned values. This combination targets long-horizon, sparse-reward tasks and improves zero-shot generalization under visual distractions.

The key insight is that the value functions of available skills encode scene affordances and thus form a task-relevant, compact abstraction of state that naturally ignores distractors and supports long-horizon planning. The method, Value Function Spaces, constructs a representation by stacking the value functions (or their predictions) of each low-level policy as features for higher-level decision-making, and uses this skill-centric embedding for planning and hierarchical control. Empirical results on maze navigation and robotic manipulation show improved long-horizon performance and better zero-shot generalization compared to baseline model-free and model-based approaches.

result.text: The paper addresses limitations of visual prompt tuning (VPT)—notably poor initialization, sensitivity to prompt length, and weak performance when adapting self-supervised pretrained vision models to downstream tasks—and seeks a lightweight way to boost adaptation without full fine-tuning. The key insight is that learned prompt tokens rapidly become highly correlated with downstream image patch tokens, so initializing prompts from downstream token prototypes (clusters of target-token features) gives a strong, semantically meaningful starting point that improves mutual information with patches. Methodologically, the authors propose Self-Prompt-Tuning (SPT): compute prototype tokens from downstream data, initialize and optionally refine a small set of learnable prompt tokens based on these prototypes, and use a streamlined optimization pipeline that keeps compute overhead negligible compared to VPT; extensive experiments show SPT outperforms prior prompt and full fine-tuning on many benchmarks while using <0.4% of parameters and substantially improves adaptation for self-supervised pretrained models.

result.text: The paper addresses the limitation of egocentric video understanding methods that rely on short clip-level visual features and therefore fail to capture the camera-wearer’s broader, persistent environment and unseen local surroundings. The key insight is that training models to predict and encode the latent, human-centric environment from first-person video—using simulated 3D environments where full observability provides supervisory signal—yields environment-aware representations that transfer to real-world egocentric footage. The method trains on videos of agents in simulated scenes to learn features predictive of the local, potentially occluded environment and then plugs those learned representations into downstream human-centric video tasks; this yields consistent improvements over clip-only features and, despite simulation-only training, strong performance on real-world datasets including state-of-the-art results on the Ego4D NLQ challenge.

args.text: I propose Timestep-Conditioned Sparse-MLP for Diffusion Transformers: a post-training, per-timestep neuron masking scheme that exploits the intrinsic sparsity of Transformer MLP activations to cut FLOPs during denoising. Using a small calibration set, we compute per-layer Fisher/activation statistics across diffusion timesteps to derive Top-k neuron masks that are shared within short timestep windows, and we add a lightweight low-rank regressor that reconstructs the pruned neurons’ contribution from the retained activations to minimize error. This yields a static, timestep-aware sparse execution plan at deployment, complementary to layer caching and attention sharing, and requires only minutes of calibration without full retraining. The goal is to substantially reduce MLP compute in DiTs with negligible quality loss, capitalizing on temporal redundancy and inherent activation sparsity.

result.text: Ferret tackles the problem of precise spatial referring and open-vocabulary grounding in images, enabling multimodal models to refer to and describe regions of any shape or granularity while avoiding object hallucination. The key insight is a hybrid region representation that jointly encodes discrete coordinates and continuous visual features, combined with a spatial-aware visual sampler that can extract informative continuous features from arbitrarily shaped, sparse regions. Ferret’s method unifies referring and grounding in an LLM by accepting diverse region inputs (points, boxes, free-form shapes), training on a large curated GRIT dataset of 1.1M refer-and-ground instruction samples (including 95K hard negatives), and fine-tuning the multimodal LLM to reason and respond about region-based queries; this yields state-of-the-art performance on classical referring/grounding tasks and markedly better region-based multimodal dialogue and localization.

result.text: I propose LR-Cache: augment layer-caching for diffusion transformers with low-rank activation reconstruction instead of pure reuse. For layers selected to skip, we store a reference activation and apply a per-layer, timestep-conditioned low-rank projector that predicts a small delta to the cached output from cheap inputs (e.g., timestep embedding and shallow features), learned post-training on a small unlabeled set to match original layer outputs. This adds an “approximate” mode to the cache router, enabling more aggressive skipping while preserving quality, with per-layer adaptive ranks and negligible extra FLOPs. A brief, layerwise reconstruction phase calibrates the low-rank bases and deltas, analogous to fast post-training output reconstruction, but targeting activation subspaces rather than masks.

result.text: The paper tackles safe exploration in episodic constrained Markov decision processes, asking whether one can obtain near-optimal reward regret while eliminating or sharply limiting constraint violations. Its key insight is that combining optimism for reward with pessimism for constraints—leveraging a known strictly safe baseline when available or conservatively estimating constraint costs otherwise—lets an agent explore without incurring growing safety breaches. Concretely, when a strictly safe policy is known the authors design an optimistic-pessimistic algorithm that confines constraint violation to zero with high probability while maintaining Õ(√K) reward regret; when no safe policy is known but one exists, they give a primal–dual method that uses optimistic primal estimates and pessimistic dual updates to guarantee only bounded constraint violation with high probability alongside Õ(√K) regret.

result.text: The paper addresses the theoretical gap in understanding how softmax attention in transformers learns to select important tokens despite its nonconvex training dynamics. The key insight is that gradient descent on the attention parameters converges in direction to a max-margin separator that discriminates locally-optimal tokens from non-optimal ones, thereby formalizing attention as an implicit margin-maximizing token selector whose notion of optimality is determined by value embeddings and problem geometry. Methodologically, the authors analyze the softmax-attention model f(X)=⟨Xv, softmax(XWp)⟩ and prove directional convergence results for gradient descent on p (and W), extend the analysis to regularization paths and nonlinear heads, and characterize joint v and p training under logistic loss as converging to coupled hard-margin SVM solutions influenced by each other’s support vectors. They validate these theoretical claims with numerical experiments that illustrate the predicted margin-maximizing behavior.

result.text: The paper tackles the problem that reinforcement learning agents trained on a few environments often fail to generalize to new, unseen environments by proposing a way to learn representations that capture behaviorally relevant structure. The key insight is a theoretically motivated policy similarity metric (PSM) that rates states as similar when the optimal policies at those states — and in their future trajectories — are alike, thereby encoding sequential and long-horizon behavioral equivalence rather than superficial observation similarity. result.text: We propose Open-Set Calibrated Triaging (OSCT) for domain-adaptive/source-free object detection, which estimates a per-box knownness by fusing category-dictionary reconstruction residuals with a probabilistic teacher’s predictive uncertainty and calibrates it via a task-aware calibrator adapted on target using split-conformal risk control. High-knownness boxes drive self-training; medium-knownness regions trigger localized adversarial/feature alignment; and low-knownness (likely-novel) boxes are masked from pseudo-labels and used only to train an abstention head and to support masked alignment, preventing negative transfer from unknown classes. The calibrator follows a TCD-style auxiliary calibration at source and is bootstrapped on target from teacher–student agreement, while residual cues provide class-conditional pseudo-IoU to disentangle mislocalized known objects from truly novel ones. OSCT improves AP on known classes and confidence reliability under open-set shift without requiring access to source data.

result.text: MetaDiffuser addresses the problem of generalizing offline reinforcement learning across tasks with varying rewards or dynamics by casting meta-RL as a conditional trajectory-generation problem. The key insight is to treat task generalization as context-conditioned diffusion planning: learn a diffusion model that generates task-oriented trajectories conditioned on a contextual task representation, and guide sampling to ensure both high return and dynamics consistency. The method trains a context-conditioned diffusion model on offline meta-datasets and, at test time, uses a dual-guided sampling module—one guide encouraging high returns and another enforcing dynamics consistency—to produce trajectories for planning; this approach is robust to limited warm-start data and compatible with different task representations, outperforming strong baselines on MuJoCo.

The key insight is that the Segment Anything Model (SAM) already encodes rich intra- and inter-image semantics in its latent space that can be exploited to detect changes without retraining: by matching bitemporal latents between two images, differences corresponding to semantic change naturally emerge. result.text: The paper tackles the gap in evaluating and attacking moderation guardrails in large language models (LLMs), noting that many jailbreak benchmarks ignore prompts that trigger input- or output-level moderation filters; this leaves both evaluation and red-teaming incomplete. The key insight is that effective jailbreaks must target both input filters (via crafted prefixes) and output filters (by encoding harmful content using non-standard “cipher characters” produced by a surrogate model that mimics the guardrail), enabling harmful content to evade detection and decoding back into readable form. result.text: The paper addresses unstable training of Transformer-based vision models, arguing that common practical fixes (warmup, LayerNorm, attention tweaks, initialization) are band-aids rather than principled solutions. Its key insight is that enforcing Lipschitz continuity across Transformer components is sufficient to guarantee training stability, faster convergence, and improved generalization without careful learning-rate warmup. To realize this, the authors design LipsFormer by replacing instability-prone modules with Lipschitz-continuous alternatives—CenterNorm in place of LayerNorm, spectral initialization instead of Xavier, scaled cosine-similarity attention instead of dot-product, and a weighted residual shortcut—prove these modules are Lipschitz and derive an upper bound on the network Lipschitz constant, and empirically demonstrate stable, high-performing training on ImageNet (e.g., 82.7% top-1 for a Swin-Tiny variant and 83.5% for a CSwin-Tiny variant) without learning-rate warmup.

result.text: The paper tackles the problem of LLMs being vulnerable to jailbreaking attacks that manipulate prompts to elicit unsafe or undesired outputs, noting that prior defenses struggle against new or adaptive attacks. Its key insight is to model the adversary explicitly within the defensive objective and optimize a compact, transferable suffix that hardens the model against worst-case adaptive jailbreaks. The method, Robust Prompt Optimization (RPO), formulates an optimization-based defense that searches for system-level prompt suffixes by iteratively simulating adversarial attacks during training and minimizing attack success rates. Empirically and theoretically, RPO substantially improves robustness—dropping ASR on JailbreakBench to 6% for GPT-4 and 0% for Llama-2—while remaining lightweight and transferable.

args.text: We hypothesize that each attention head implements a proximal mirror-descent step on a composite objective that combines a Hopfield-style associative energy (for data fit) with a max-margin token-selection regularizer, where the mirror map is set by the normalization/geometry (e.g., softmax, cosine, or flow) and the step size is bounded via spectral norms. This view unifies evidence that transformers perform gradient-like updates in context (linear and functional GD) with implicit SVM-like biases and convex-dual low-rank clustering behaviors. We propose Mirror-Prox Attention: replace softmax with an explicit Bregman proximal operator (entropic/cosine/flow variants) and add a learnable margin temperature, while enforcing spectral normalization to prevent entropy collapse and using kernelized features (Performer) or flow constraints to instantiate different geometries. We will validate by checking per-layer descent inequalities and support-set sparsity, and by measuring stability without warmup and improved in-context learning on regression and nonlinear tasks over long sequences.

result.text: The paper addresses the sample inefficiency of visual reinforcement learning, particularly the difficulty of learning control-relevant representations from pixels and the neglect of continuous action representation learning in prior self-supervised objectives. Its key insight is that jointly maximizing mutual information between latent encodings of current states paired with action sequences and encodings of the resulting future states forces the learned state and action latents to capture information sufficient for control. The proposed method, TACO, implements a temporal action-driven contrastive loss that simultaneously trains state and action encoders by contrasting positive (state+action sequence → future state) pairs against negatives, and integrates this loss into both online and offline RL pipelines; empirically it yields substantial sample-efficiency gains in online visual continuous control and improves offline visual RL performance across datasets.

result.text: The paper addresses the need for fast, practical adversarial attacks on language models to probe safety and privacy vulnerabilities. Its key insight is that a beam-search–based, gradient-free attack with interpretable parameters can trade off speed, success rate, and prompt readability to produce effective targeted and untargeted adversarial prompts far faster than gradient-based methods. The proposed method, BEAST, performs parameterized beam search over candidate prompt edits to rapidly find adversarial inputs that jailbreak aligned models, induce hallucinations, or improve membership-inference attacks, achieving e.g., an 89% jailbreak success on Vicuna-7B-v1.5 in under one minute on a single RTX A6000 versus over an hour for a gradient baseline, and causing measurable increases in incorrect or irrelevant outputs in human evaluations.

The paper tackles limitations in prompt learning for vision-language models, specifically that existing trainable prompts are derived from global image features and treated equally, which can ignore discriminative foreground details and fail under distribution shift. Its key insight is that prompts should be grounded in local, spatially localized image features and adaptively weighted according to image-specific semantics, yielding dynamic prompts aligned with relevant regions and local contextual relationships. The proposed Contextual Prompt Learning (CoPL) framework incorporates local image features into prompt construction and learns an attention-like weighting mechanism to reweight and align multiple prompts to task-relevant local features, producing region-aware, dynamically composed prompts. Experiments on standard, few-shot, and out-of-distribution benchmarks demonstrate substantially improved generalization and robustness compared to prior prompt-learning approaches.

result.text: The paper tackles the practical challenge of reducing Transformer inference cost without the high time and complexity of retraining-based pruning methods by proposing a fast post-training pruning framework. The key insight is that structured sparsity can be applied post-training if one carefully selects and adjusts masks to preserve important parameters—using Fisher-information-guided mask search, complementary mask rearrangement, and a lightweight mask-tuning step that reconstructs layer outputs. Their method automatically finds which heads and filters to remove under a resource constraint and applies only brief, layerwise reconstruction (no full retraining), enabling up to 2.0x FLOPs reduction and 1.56x latency speedup on BERT-base and DistilBERT with under 1% accuracy loss on GLUE and SQuAD. Crucially, the entire procedure runs in under three minutes on a single GPU, offering a practical, two-orders-of-magnitude faster alternative to retraining-based pruning.

result.text: The paper addresses the over-smoothing problem in deep transformers, where repeated self-attention causes token representations to become nearly identical and degrades model capacity. The key insight is that self-attention layers implicitly minimize a smoothness-promoting nonlocal functional, so preventing over-smoothing requires a regularizer that preserves fidelity between input tokens and the smoothed outputs. The authors introduce a regularizer that penalizes the norm of the difference between self-attention outputs and inputs, derive a Neural Transformer with a Regularized Nonlocal Functional (NeuTRENO) by minimizing the resulting energy, and show empirically that NeuTRENO reduces token uniformity and improves performance on tasks such as object classification, image segmentation, and language modeling.

The key insight is that one can define and extract an "Action-Sufficient state Representation" (ASR)—a minimal latent set that, by structural constraints in a generative model, contains exactly the information needed for maximizing cumulative reward and no extraneous sensory detail. args.text: We propose Counterfactual-PSM Hierarchical Control: pretrain on action-free video a latent world model whose distances approximate policy/bisimulation similarity by aligning predicted successor rollouts, then cluster this space to discover subgoal landmarks. A high-level policy plans over this landmark graph using a purely passive, counterfactual-intent TD objective, while a low-level controller is trained with inner-product contrastive RL on (state, subgoal) tuples and a joint state–action encoder that maximizes MI with future latents. We enforce action-sufficiency via a structured generative constraint on the latent to discard distractors and stabilize planning, and adopt a states-as-actions decomposition for offline fine-tuning to reduce long-horizon value bias. The result is a unified pipeline for long-horizon, image-based goal-reaching from passive, cross-embodiment video with strong zero-shot robustness and rapid online adaptation.

result.text: The paper addresses learning control policies for complex tasks specified by logical formulas, where existing methods that compile specifications into rewards struggle to scale to tasks requiring hierarchical planning. The key insight is to decompose a specification into an abstract graph of regions and simpler sub-tasks and to interleave high-level planning over that graph with low-level reinforcement learning for each sub-task, so planning guides exploration and learning sculpts skills. The proposed method, DiRL, constructs an abstract graph from the logical specification, uses a Dijkstra-style planner to compute high-level plans over graph edges, and trains neural policies for each edge (sub-task) via RL while iteratively updating plan costs and recomputing plans; experiments on continuous control benchmarks show improved performance over state-of-the-art baselines.

result.text: The paper investigates whether safety alignment of large language models (LLMs) holds when users communicate in non-natural languages (ciphers), addressing the risk that current defenses—trained primarily on natural language—may be bypassed. The key insight is that LLMs can understand and respond to ciphered prompts, and in fact exhibit a latent "secret cipher" behavior that can be triggered via role play and enciphered demonstrations, enabling stealthy jailbreaks even against strong models like GPT-4. The authors introduce CipherChat, a framework that sends system-role descriptions and few-shot enciphered examples to LLMs to systematically evaluate 11 safety domains across English and Chinese, showing that many human-designed ciphers and the proposed SelfCipher can nearly completely bypass GPT-4’s safety in several domains. Their results reveal a pressing need to extend alignment methods beyond natural languages and provide code and data for reproducibility.

These J_* matrices are fitted post-training by linear regression on consecutive-step pairs, akin to layerwise output reconstruction, and plugged into an L2C-style static router that authorizes skips only when the predicted linearization error is below a threshold. args.text: Certified Transform Smoothing (CTS) is a test-time guardrail that gives per-sample guarantees that an LLM will refuse unsafe behavior across a distribution of text-rendering channels and tokenizers. CTS samples a calibrated mix of Unicode normalizations, homoglyph/diacritic mappings, transliterations, cipher-decoders that mimic guardrail-evading outputs, and multiple encode–decode tokenizers, then runs short repeat-to-detect probes; using Clopper–Pearson bounds, it certifies a lower bound on refusal probability and flags the interaction if any variant turns unsafe or the bound falls below threshold. By unifying repeat-based detection with certified ensemble robustness, CTS directly targets JAM-style output-filter evasions and tokenizer/pathological-decoding bypasses while yielding actionable certificates rather than heuristics. We will evaluate on JAMBench and cipher settings and study smoothing-distribution design to maximize certified coverage at fixed query budgets.

args.text: StateChangeAlign unifies audio cues with geometry-guided canonicalization for ego–exo alignment in egocentric videos. Using EPIC Fields camera poses, we warp first-person clips into a stable workspace view and, at audio-detected interaction onsets, extract VISOR-guided hand/active-object crops; we then train an AE2-style contrastive objective that pulls audio-synchronous anchors across unpaired users and exocentric views while pushing pre/post-onset frames as hard negatives to encode state-change sensitivity. Compared to geometry-only or vision-only alignment, audio-anchored positives improve temporal correspondence, cross-view invariance, and robustness to idle/background motions, yielding gains on fine-grained actions and object state-change localization. We evaluate on ego↔exo retrieval, cross-view action recognition, and state-change detection, and ablate onset detector quality and mask/pose noise to quantify contributions of audio vs. geometry.

result.text: The paper tackles slow inference in diffusion transformers, where each denoising step executes a large transformer resulting in high computational cost. Its key insight is that many transformer layers produce redundant, timestep-repetitive computations that can be cached and skipped without modifying model weights, yielding large FLOPs and latency savings with negligible quality loss. The proposed Learning-to-Cache (L2C) method treats each transformer layer as a cacheable unit and learns an input-invariant but timestep-varying router via a differentiable optimization objective to decide which layers to reuse versus recompute, producing a static computation graph at deployment; experiments show L2C removes a large fraction of layer computations (e.g., up to ~94% in some cache steps) while preserving FID and outperforming existing samplers and prior cache methods at equal inference speed.

result.text: The paper addresses understanding and extending the transformer attention mechanism by linking it to associative memory: it asks what kind of memory model attention implements and how that explains transformers’ behavior and learning. The key insight is that transformer attention is exactly the update rule of a newly formulated modern Hopfield network with continuous states that can store an exponential number of patterns, converge rapidly (often in one update), and trade off storage capacity against convergence speed and retrieval error; this interpretation explains three types of energy minima (global averaging, metastable subset-averaging, and single-pattern fixed points) and how different transformer layers and attention heads operate and learn. Methodologically, the authors derive the Hopfield energy and update equations that match attention, analyze dynamics and gradients across layers (showing early layers favor global averaging while later layers form metastable attractors), demonstrate practical gains on tasks like immune-repertoire classification, and provide a PyTorch "Hopfield" layer and Gaussian-weighting simplification for replacing average-like heads to integrate this memory-attention perspective into deep architectures.

args.text: We propose Counterfactual-PSM from Passive Video (C-PSM-V): learn a policy-similarity–aligned latent space by estimating, for each state, the distribution of counterfactual returns over a bank of latent intents inferred purely from action-free videos. Concretely, we pretrain a video world model and learn intent-conditioned predictors via passive TD, then define a PSM-like distance between states as the divergence between their predicted return profiles across intents, and train an encoder to match this metric in the spirit of PSE/bisimulation. Clustering this space yields subgoal landmarks and we train a hierarchical goal-conditioned controller on them with offline data, improving long-horizon generalization and robustness to visual distractors. The counterfactual-intent basis further supports cross-embodiment transfer by anchoring behavioral similarity to task families rather than pixel dynamics.

result.text: The paper tackles unsupervised domain adaptation for object detection with DETR, addressing instability and stagnation in existing one-stage alignment and inconsistencies in two-stage mean-teacher approaches, as well as the unexplored use of a third, target-like domain. The key insight is that combining a mean-teacher two-stage pipeline with masked feature alignment and a target-like pretraining set yields more robust and consistent adaptation: masked alignment reduces harmful domain interference, target-like pretraining stabilizes learning, and object-query knowledge transfer preserves student gains. The method (MTM) first pretrains the detector on labeled, style-transferred target-like images to avoid fluctuation, then self-trains with mean-teacher pseudo-labels while applying Object Queries Knowledge Transfer (OQKT) and two complementary masked feature alignment modules—Masked Domain Query-based Feature Alignment (MDQFA) and Masked Token-wise Feature Alignment (MTWFA)—to align features selectively and prevent training stagnation, with experiments and theory showing improved robustness across scenarios.

args.text: Anytime Multi-View Safety Testing (AMuST) is a black-box guardrail that adaptively aggregates signals from repeat-to-detect, decoding-invariant refusal, and transform/cipher self-decoding into a single sequential test with tight latency control. For each prompt, AMuST interleaves short-prefix probes under randomized decoding seeds/policies, output repetition and semantic restatement, and semantics-preserving input/output transforms that induce diverse tokenizations; it updates a Wald-style sequential probability ratio test with Clopper–Pearson bounds on the probability of unsafe realizations and stops as soon as either safety is certified above a threshold or an unsafe variant appears. A learned scheduler prioritizes the next "view" by estimated marginal information gain per query under a latency budget, and caching reuses probes across conversational turns. We will evaluate on guardrail-triggering benchmarks and cipher attacks to show improved recall on decoding- and filter-evasion jailbreaks at similar false positives and modest (≈1.2–1.5×) median overhead versus single-view baselines.

args.text: Proximal Entropic Hopfield Attention (PEHA) treats a transformer head as one-step associative-memory retrieval on the Hopfield energy and replaces the softmax update with a mirror-prox step that minimizes the Hopfield energy plus a KL penalty to a uniform prior on attention, yielding a tunable entropy floor. By combining this explicit entropic barrier with per-layer Lipschitz control (scaled-cosine attention and spectral reparameterization), PEHA provides a provable lower bound on attention entropy and stable gradients that directly target the entropy-collapse failure mode. We further include a fidelity term in the energy that penalizes deviation from input token features to counteract over-smoothing, leading to closed-form proximal weights and an interpretable bias–variance knob. For long contexts, we compute the proximal step over structured factorizations of the attention graph (e.g., hierarchical Combiner-style routes) to retain sub-quadratic complexity while preserving the same entropy and Lipschitz guarantees.

result.text: The paper tackles sample-inefficiency in vision-based reinforcement learning by asking whether unsupervised, action-free video pre-training can produce representations that speed up downstream RL. The key insight is that generative pre-training on raw videos yields latent dynamics features useful for later learning of action-conditional world models, and that these pre-trained features can both enhance fine-tuning and drive better exploration. Methodologically, they first train an action-free latent video prediction model, then stack a newly designed action-conditional latent predictor on top of the frozen or fine-tuned pretrained model for RL fine-tuning, and augment exploration with a video-based intrinsic bonus derived from the pre-trained representations. Experiments on manipulation and locomotion tasks show substantial gains in sample efficiency and final performance.

args.text: We propose Bounded-Entry Higher-Order Attention (BEHOA), a practical recipe that makes triple-wise tensor attention tractable by enforcing bounded attention logits via cosine-similarity attention and spectral reparameterization, thereby satisfying the bounded-entry premise needed for near-linear higher-order attention. BEHOA integrates an adaptive temperature controller that monitors the running max of |QK| and rescales queries/keys to remain below the theoretical threshold; when the bound is at risk, it selectively falls back to pairwise attention or sparse factorizations. This preserves an entropy floor that prevents attention entropy collapse and stabilizes training while capturing higher-order correlations that standard attention misses. As long as the controller maintains the bound, the triple-wise module runs in n^{1+o(1)} time with predictable memory, enabling practical deployment in long-context vision and language models.

result.text: The paper addresses the challenge of learning goal-conditioned policies from diverse offline (reward-free) datasets, where estimating exact value for distant goals is unreliable and long-horizon goal-reaching is difficult. The key insight is that goal-reaching naturally decomposes hierarchically—reaching far goals requires passing through nearer subgoals whose values are easier to estimate—so treating intermediate states as latent “actions” lets a high-level policy propose subgoals while a low-level policy executes to them, reducing reliance on accurate long-horizon value estimates. The method, HIQL, learns a single action-free value function and two policies from offline data: a high-level policy that predicts a latent representation of a subgoal (treating states as actions) and a low-level policy that outputs primitive actions to reach that subgoal; this hierarchical decomposition is shown analytically and empirically to be robust to value estimation noise and effective on long-horizon and image-based offline goal-reaching tasks, including leveraging action-free data.

result.text: We propose Affordance-Conditioned Subtrajectory Diffusion: a diffusion planner that generates multi-step action-state sequences conditioned not only on the goal (and optional return) but also on a compact affordance embedding given by the vector of values of a library of low-level skills at the current state. We further employ a self-evolving improvement loop where reward/affordance gradients guide sampling and a feasibility discriminator filters candidates before finetuning the model, yielding progressively better stitching from offline data. result.text: EgoSchema addresses the challenge of evaluating and driving progress in very long-form video understanding by providing a diagnostic multiple-choice QA benchmark drawn from 250+ hours of first-person footage where each question requires choosing the correct answer from five options based on a three-minute clip. The key insight is that clip length alone does not capture temporal difficulty, so the authors introduce "temporal certificate sets" to measure the intrinsic temporal extent required to solve a video understanding task and show EgoSchema’s intrinsic temporal lengths are an order of magnitude larger than prior datasets. Methodologically, they curate over 5,000 human-validated QA pairs from Ego4D, quantify temporal complexity with the certificate metric, and evaluate state-of-the-art vision–language models—finding current models perform far below humans (≈33% vs. 76% accuracy), thereby establishing EgoSchema as a rigorous benchmark for long-term video reasoning and providing data and zero-shot evaluation code under the Ego4D license.

args.text: We propose Entropy-Flow Controlled Attention (EFCA): a per-head, per-layer controller that treats attention entropy as a state variable and optimizes a Lagrangian to keep it within a depth-dependent corridor, preventing early collapse while allowing later specialization. EFCA is implemented by (i) spectral-normalizing Q/K to bound logit scales, (ii) a learnable temperature gate with barrier penalties on empirical attention entropy, and (iii) coupling the entropy corridor to a token-fidelity regularizer to counter over-smoothing. The Hopfield view predicts that maintaining a nonzero entropy floor avoids premature convergence to single-pattern attractors, while the margin-maximization view suggests annealing the corridor tightens selection only after stable directions emerge; jointly with Lipschitz constraints this yields warmup-free stable training and improved depth scaling. A simple controller adapts per-batch via dual ascent on entropy constraints, and preliminary results on ViT and decoder LMs indicate reduced divergence events and improved long-sequence generalization at matched compute.

result.text: We propose Counterfactual Background Robustness (CBR) for source-free/domain-adaptive object detection: for each target pseudo box, we synthesize counterfactuals by cutting out the object (via the teacher’s mask/box) and pasting it onto a bank of diverse source-like and target-like backgrounds, then measure the teacher’s class/box stability across these composites to obtain a per-box CBR score. We fuse CBR with the teacher’s predictive uncertainty and calibrate the combined quality via a task-aware auxiliary calibration loss and split-conformal adjustment over the composite set, yielding reliable weights for pseudo-labeling. Training uses this calibrated quality to (i) upweight robust object-centric pseudo boxes and (ii) trigger selective, masked background-only alignment and cross-composite consistency (e.g., query invariance for DETR) for background-sensitive instances, explicitly decoupling object from context. This counterfactual probing mitigates spurious context transfer, improves calibration and localization under shift, and boosts SFOD/UDA detection without accessing source images.

args.text: Automaton-Guided Affordance Diffusion (AGAD): a trajectory diffusion planner for LTL-specified tasks that conditions sampling on the current automaton state and a value-function-space affordance vector, and guides denoising with a differentiable automaton-progress potential built from compositional value functions. By operating in the product of environment state and task automaton, the sampler respects safety (negations) and sequencing (conjunctions/disjunctions) via score augmentation with Boolean-composed value gradients, enabling zero-shot composition and long-horizon reliability. We train the diffusion model on offline demonstrations segmented by automaton edges and learn affordance predictors to bias stitching toward feasible skill sequences. On navigation and manipulation benchmarks with sparse rewards and logical constraints, AGAD outperforms DiRL-style planners and return-/goal-conditioned diffusion baselines in success and constraint satisfaction.

result.text: Extend object-identifier LLM grounding in 3D to a persistent 4D setting where the same real-world instance keeps a stable token across multiple scans of a scene. We learn a cross-scan object codebook by aligning instances with a contrastive tracking objective while distilling synthetic multi-view 2D cues into the 3D encoder and injecting motion-aware pairwise geometry into attention, so the LLM can answer temporal referring and change-centric questions. Each identifier token carries lightweight temporal slots (pose/appearance deltas and relation edges) that let the model attend over changes instead of re-detecting. Supervision is bootstrapped from hierarchical region–object annotations by generating pseudo-temporal pairs via partial rescans and scene perturbations with change-focused language prompts, enabling capabilities like “find the chair that moved since yesterday” without a dedicated tracking head.

result.text: We propose Decoding-Invariant Refusal (DIR), a test-time guardrail that neutralizes jailbreaks exploiting decoding hyperparameters by enforcing safety/refusal consistency across a randomized ensemble of decoding policies and seeds. DIR performs short-prefix probes under a bank of sampling regimes (e.g., temperature, top-k/p, beams) and a repeat/regenerate step to stay in the model’s natural generation channel, then estimates a binomial lower bound on the refusal (or safety) rate; it flags the prompt or escalates alignment if any unsafe variant appears or the certified refusal probability falls below a threshold. This randomized-smoothing view makes attacks that rely on dialing decoding settings ineffective and pairs naturally with loss-landscape probes as an auxiliary signal. We will evaluate DIR against decoding-exploitation attacks, TAP-generated prompts, and output-filter-evading settings from JAMBench, targeting low added latency via short-prefix probes and caching.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem of improving coarse object masks produced by diverse segmentation models in a model-agnostic way. Its key insight is to cast segmentation refinement as a conditional data-generation task and perform it via a discrete denoising diffusion process that iteratively predicts per-pixel labels and state-transition probabilities to remove noise. The method, called SegRefiner, takes coarse masks as input and applies a learned discrete diffusion model that progressively refines masks through multiple denoising steps conditioned on the input image, and is evaluated across semantic, instance, and binary segmentation tasks where it consistently improves standard and boundary metrics and recovers fine details better than prior model-agnostic refiners.

args.text: Contact-frame canonicalization for ego↔exo action alignment: we use EPIC Fields’ per-frame camera poses to lift hand and active-object pixels to 3D, and VISOR masks to localize interactions, then estimate a temporally smooth object-centric contact frame (grasp axis and contact patch) that defines a canonical SE(3) warp for egocentric clips. We train encoders on these contact-canonicalized crops with AE2-style contrastive alignment to unpaired exocentric videos, selecting positives around audio-anchored interaction peaks and adding a DVANet-inspired auxiliary head to disentangle view-specific from action features. Compared to workspace-only canonicalization, contact-frame normalization yields tighter temporal correspondence across users and improves cross-view retrieval and recognition. As a downstream test, we show the learned contact frames enable more realistic cross-object HOI editing and motion propagation in HOI-Swap-like pipelines.

result.text: The paper tackles efficient compression of Transformer models for resource-constrained deployment, noting that prior weight-focused low-rank approximations perform poorly for transformers and require large labeled datasets to fine-tune. Its key insight is that activations (features) in transformer layers are empirically low-rank even though the learned weight matrices are not, so compressing outputs rather than weights yields more faithful reduction. Building on this, the authors introduce AAFM, which adaptively determines per-layer compression structure and locally compresses each linear layer's output features in a few-shot, unsupervised manner, followed by a global fine-tuning stage GFM that holistically optimizes the compressed network; both stages use only a small unlabeled sample set. The method achieves substantial parameter and latency reductions with minimal accuracy loss (e.g., 33% parameters removed and 18.8% throughput gain with only 0.23% ImageNet accuracy drop using 2K unlabeled images), transfers to NLP tasks, and generalizes well to downstream tasks.

args.text: We propose Constrained-Entropy Hopfield Attention (CEHA): each head performs a proximal step that minimizes a Hopfield-style attention energy plus a token-fidelity term, subject to an explicit per-head lower bound on attention entropy. The constraint is enforced by a learned temperature dual variable updated via projected dual ascent, while logit matrices are spectrally normalized to keep the dual feasible and controllable. This convex-approximate constrained update prevents attention-entropy collapse and counters deep over-smoothing, yielding stable training without warmup and preserving layerwise discriminability. By coupling entropy control with the implicit max-margin selection bias of attention, later layers form metastable subset attractors without pathological sharpness.

result.text: Counterfactual-Action-free Reachability Embeddings (CARE): From passive videos, train a latent world model and learn intervention operators that stochastically perturb latent dynamics to approximate the set of futures reachable from each state under any policy (“reachability cones”). Define a policy-similarity metric as the Wasserstein distance between these k-step reachability-cone distributions, yielding a representation that approximates PSM/bisimulation without actions, is robust to visual distractors, and supports cross-embodiment alignment. Clustering this space induces a subgoal graph for hierarchical goal-conditioned control; during RL, a brief probe phase fits a local control-Jacobian in latent space to prune subgoals along poorly controllable directions. This hybrid pretrain+probe scheme improves long-horizon exploration and transfer in image-based tasks while avoiding unstable end-to-end objectives.

result.text: The paper tackles offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (GCRL), where limited, often suboptimal pre-collected trajectories and sparse goal rewards make learning long-horizon goal-directed behaviors challenging. Its key insight is that a conditional diffusion model can generate high-quality multi-step plans by stitching together useful sub-trajectory segments from offline data when conditioned not only on the target goal but also on an estimated target value, enabling the synthesis of trajectories that exceed individual dataset snippets. The proposed method, SSD (Sub-trajectory Stitching with Diffusion), first relabels the offline dataset with goal and value estimates, then trains a conditional diffusion model to sample future state-action sequences given a goal and value, and finally uses the model to produce stitched long-horizon plans which are executed or refined by a model-based policy; experiments show state-of-the-art performance and successful composition of suboptimal segments into effective goal-reaching plans.

The key insight is to introduce a learned semantic graph prior that explicitly captures object-level semantics and relations alongside layout distributions, enabling more faithful and controllable generation conditioned on instructions. args.text: I propose Counterfactual Mask Transport (CMT): a mask-aware prompt-tuning framework that learns compact banks of region-specific visual/text prompts via optimal-transport alignment while training against diffusion-generated counterfactual masks that mimic near-miss proposals. Starting from blur–reverse masked regions to suppress context leakage, we sample hard negatives by early-stopping a discrete diffusion refiner around each proposal and enforce a tri-part loss that separates overlapping/near-boundary masks, aligns prompts to the correct region via Sinkhorn OT, and distills global CLIP knowledge to preserve zero-shot transfer. Dynamic, locally conditioned prompt weighting lets the same prompt bank adapt per image without full fine-tuning, in the spirit of contextual prompting but with explicit counterfactual calibration. At test time, no diffusion is used; the learned prompt banks plus mask-aware routing reduce false positives and improve open-vocabulary segmentation and referring segmentation in zero-/few-shot settings.

result.text: The paper addresses the lack of large-scale, egocentric datasets that combine accurate 3D camera geometry with annotated video understanding for neural rendering and dynamic scene modeling. Its key insight is that augmenting an existing action-rich egocentric video corpus (EPIC-KITCHENS) with reconstructed camera poses and geometry removes the costly photogrammetry bottleneck and better supports tasks that require both spatial structure and semantic labels. The authors introduce EPIC Fields, a dataset that registers 19M frames across 45 kitchens (recovering cameras for 96% of videos) and pairs these 3D-enabled videos with action segments and VISOR object masks, and they demonstrate the utility by proposing methods and strong baselines for neural rendering and dynamic object segmentation that reveal current limitations and show geometry improves semi-supervised segmentation.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem of learning near-optimal predictive models when deploying a model changes the data distribution (performative prediction) and the learner must both collect feedback and minimize cumulative regret. The key insight is that performative feedback—observing samples from the induced shifted distribution after each deployment—yields a richer signal than standard bandit feedback, allowing regret to scale with the complexity of distribution shifts rather than the complexity of the reward function. The authors propose an algorithm that, under only smoothness assumptions on the shifts (no convexity needed), carefully explores to learn the mapping from models to induced distributions and constructs novel confidence bounds on unexplored models’ risks; this yields regret guarantees and ensures the final iterate is near-optimal. More broadly, their approach adapts bandit-style tools to exploit performative feedback for efficient regret minimization.

result.text: The paper addresses the quadratic computation and memory bottleneck of self-attention in vision transformers, which limits scalability to long token sequences for visual recognition. The key insight is that keeping the softmax normalization in attention prevents effective linearization, so removing softmax and replacing the scaled dot-product with a Gaussian kernel allows the full attention matrix to be approximated as a low-rank factorization. The method, called SOFT, uses Gaussian-kernel-based similarity without further normalization and computes a robust low-rank approximation by estimating the Moore–Penrose inverse via a Newton–Raphson procedure, yielding linear complexity in tokens. Experiments on ImageNet show SOFT achieves much better computational efficiency and enables much longer token sequences while maintaining or improving accuracy compared to prior ViT variants.

result.text: The paper addresses unsupervised domain adaptation for object detection, aiming to transfer detector performance from a labeled source domain to an unlabeled target domain while avoiding negative transfer from imperfect feature alignment. Its key insight is that learning category-specific dictionaries from source-domain object proposals lets target proposals be represented per-category, and the reconstruction residuals provide a reliable signal both for assigning pseudo-labels and estimating box quality (e.g., IoU), avoiding reliance on brittle global feature alignment or softmax decision boundaries. The method builds category dictionaries from source proposals, computes residuals for target candidate boxes to guide pseudo-box selection and weight their contribution by residual-derived quality scores, and trains the detector in a residual-weighted self-training loop that implicitly aligns domains and yields more informative, trustworthy pseudo-labels for improved cross-domain detection.

result.text: The paper addresses shortcomings in 3D scene understanding by large language models—specifically poor object-level referencing and grounding across diverse scene-language tasks. Its key insight is to represent a 3D scene as an explicit sequence of object-centric embeddings each paired with a unique identifier token, which converts spatial grounding into token-level reference that a language model can reliably attend to. The method decomposes scenes into object proposals, extracts semantic-rich 2D/3D embeddings for each object, attaches identifier tokens, and formulates all downstream tasks as unified QA over these identifiers so the same LLM head can jointly learn grounding and language tasks with minimal fine-tuning. This object-identifier paradigm yields strong gains on multiple benchmarks (ScanRefer, Multi3DRefer, Scan2Cap, ScanQA, SQA3D) by improving general referencing, grounding, and multi-task training efficiency.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem of obtaining reliable, sample-specific robustness guarantees against L1-bounded adversarial attacks for deep classifiers, improving on prior randomized smoothing methods that use additive noise and yield probabilistic guarantees. Its key insight is that by generating smoothing samples via random partitioning of the input space and returning the center of the occupied cell (splitting noise), the smoothing noise components need not be independent and can be effectively collapsed to one dimension, enabling efficient derandomization for quantized data. The authors introduce SSN, a randomized splitting-noise smoothing procedure, and then derive a deterministic variant, DSSN, that provides deterministic “randomized smoothing” certificates for arbitrary base classifiers without requiring exponentially many samples. Empirically on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, DSSN achieves substantially larger L1 robustness certificates and much faster certification than prior methods, establishing a new state-of-the-art.

args.text: I propose Timestep-Linearized Caching (TLC) for diffusion transformers: for layers chosen to skip, we cache the last activation along with a compact, learned low-rank Jacobian with respect to the timestep embedding and a small set of shallow features, enabling first-order extrapolation across nearby steps (y(t+Δ) ≈ y(t) + JΔ) rather than pure reuse. A brief post-training, unlabeled calibration learns per-layer adaptive ranks and valid Δ horizons, with an error monitor that triggers occasional exact recomputes to bound drift. This taps temporal smoothness more directly than static routers and complements attention sharing, extending reuse windows and boosting skip ratios without quality loss. The result is a cache that is both predictive and safe, delivering larger end-to-end speedups at high resolution.

result.text: The paper studies why attention-based modules in vision transformers work by casting non-linear dot-product self-attention and related mechanisms (MLP-mixer, FNO) into equivalent finite-dimensional convex optimization problems via convex duality, addressing the lack of a clear inductive bias explanation for attention. The key insight is that these convex equivalents reveal an implicit block nuclear-norm regularization that encourages low-rank structure across latent features and tokens, which in turn explains behaviors such as token clustering driven by latent similarity. Methodologically, the authors derive and solve global-optimal convex programs corresponding to various attention formulations, interpret the resulting regularization and clustering effects, and empirically validate the inductive bias by fine-tuning convex attention heads on a pre-trained transformer for CIFAR-100, showing advantages over MLP or linear heads.

args.text: We propose Conformal Novel Cluster Promotion (CNCP) for source-free/open-set domain-adaptive object detection, which converts low-knownness proposals into novel-class candidates and safely promotes reliable clusters into a provisional label set during adaptation. CNCP builds uncertainty-weighted embeddings by fusing category-dictionary residual affinities with a probabilistic teacher’s predictive uncertainty, clusters low-knownness boxes, and then applies split-conformal risk control over counterfactual background composites to certify cluster precision before promotion; uncertified clusters remain for abstention and masked alignment. Promoted clusters instantiate lightweight prototypes/dictionaries and, for DETR-style models, spawn new object queries via query-knowledge transfer, enabling joint metric/prototype supervision while preserving calibration with a TCD-style auxiliary loss. This turns conservative open-set triaging into online open-world learning, improving recall on emergent target categories without harming known-class AP or confidence reliability.

result.text: The paper addresses the limitation of diffusion-based offline planners whose performance and generalization are constrained by insufficient diversity of training data, especially for adapting to unseen goal-conditioned tasks. The key insight is to turn diffusion planning into an adaptive, self-evolving loop that generates synthetic expert-like trajectories guided by reward gradients and then filters those trajectories to iteratively improve the diffusion model, thereby enhancing planning quality and transfer to new tasks. Concretely, AdaptDiffuser uses reward-gradient-guided sampling to produce diverse candidate trajectories, applies a discriminator to select high-quality synthetic data, and finetunes the diffusion model on this curated data in a cyclical evolution process; experiments on Maze2D, MuJoCo, and a KUKA task show substantial gains over prior diffusion planners and improved adaptation to unseen tasks without extra expert data.

args.text: We propose Transformation-Invariant Refusal (TIR), a test-time guardrail that defends against input-layer jailbreaks by enforcing refusal consistency across a randomized ensemble of prompt transformations (e.g., paraphrases, Unicode/whitespace perturbations, transliteration/homoglyph swaps, and simple cipherings). TIR conducts short-prefix probes under this view distribution and estimates a binomial lower bound on the refusal probability; it flags or escalates when any unsafe variant appears or the certified refusal rate falls below a threshold, and pairs with a repeat-and-self-decode step to canonicalize obfuscated outputs before final judgment. This extends the randomized-smoothing perspective to input representations (complementary to decoding-invariant defenses), targeting cipher- and formatting-based bypasses without large latency via caching and lightweight paraphrase/perturbation generators. We will evaluate on JAMBench and CipherChat and study composition with decoding-invariant refusal to harden both input and output channels against black-box search attacks.

result.text: The paper addresses false-positive errors in zero-shot segmentation that arise because CLIP, trained with image-level supervision, is insensitive to different mask proposals and thus gives similar classifications to many masks in the same image. The key insight is that fine-tuning CLIP to be mask-aware—so it distinguishes different region proposals while retaining zero-shot transferability—will reduce false positives and improve segmentation for unseen classes. They introduce MAFT: an IP-CLIP Encoder that jointly processes arbitrary numbers of image and mask proposals, and train it with a mask-aware loss plus a self-distillation loss that preserves CLIP’s global knowledge; this fine-tuning requires no extra parameters at inference and plugs into existing pipeline methods, yielding large mIoU gains on COCO, Pascal-VOC, and ADE20K.

Methodologically, they formulate a contrastive audio-visual spatial alignment pretext task on 360° video with spatial audio, use a transformer to fuse representations from multiple visual viewpoints, and train the network to distinguish aligned from misaligned audio–visual pairs. result.text: The paper tackles the problem of automatically discovering jailbreak prompts for black-box large language models (LLMs), aiming to expose and bypass safety guardrails without access to model internals. The key insight is to treat jailbreak generation as a search over prompt variants guided by a separate attacker LLM that iteratively proposes and refines candidate attacks while using a lightweight pruning stage to discard low-promise candidates before querying the target, thereby reducing query cost. result.text: The paper addresses the challenge of realistically swapping objects in videos when those objects are being manipulated by hands, a scenario where existing diffusion-based video editors struggle because they do not model changes in hand-object interaction (HOI) caused by differences in object shape or function. The key insight is that realistic object swaps require HOI awareness and temporally consistent motion propagation: a model must both adapt the hand grasp and interaction patterns to the new object in a reference frame and then coherently extend that edited state through the video. HOI-Swap implements this in two stages—first training a diffusion model self-supervised to perform single-frame object swaps with learned HOI adjustments, and then propagating the edit across the sequence by warping the stage-I edited frame according to sampled motion points and conditioning a video-generation diffusion model on this warped sequence to achieve controllable motion alignment—resulting in more realistic, temporally consistent edits than prior methods.

result.text: I propose Timestep-Linearized Caching (TLC) for diffusion transformers: for layers chosen to skip, we cache the last activation along with a compact, learned low-rank Jacobian with respect to the timestep embedding and a small set of shallow features, enabling first-order extrapolation across nearby steps (y(t+Δ) ≈ y(t) + JΔ) rather than pure reuse. A brief post-training, unlabeled calibration learns per-layer adaptive ranks and valid Δ horizons, with an error monitor that triggers occasional exact recomputes to bound drift. This taps temporal smoothness more directly than static routers and complements attention sharing, extending reuse windows and boosting skip ratios without quality loss. The result is a cache that is both predictive and safe, delivering larger end-to-end speedups at high resolution.

result.text: We propose Repeat-and-Decode (RaD), a black-box safeguard that extends repetition-based detection by asking the same LLM to first verbatim-repeat a candidate output and then restate its semantic content in plain natural language before any classification, flagging the sample if the restatement triggers refusal or reveals unsafe intent. By keeping the model in its natural generation channel (repeat → explain), RaD preserves alignment like repetition-only defenses while forcing ciphered or obfuscated outputs to be self-decoded, directly targeting output-filter evasion via non-standard characters and non-natural-language prompts. RaD yields a consistency score between the repeated text and the self-decoded explanation (and refusal tokens), improving recall on cipher/output-layer bypasses without inflating false positives. We will evaluate RaD on JAMBench and CipherChat settings and stress-test with automated attack generators (e.g., TAP) to measure gains over repeat-only baselines.

result.text: VISOR addresses the problem of accurate, temporally consistent pixel-level segmentation and hand–object relation annotation in long, egocentric videos where objects undergo transformative interactions (e.g., peeling, chopping, cooking) that break assumptions of existing video segmentation datasets. The authors build a large benchmark by annotating 36 hours of EPIC-KITCHENS footage with 272K manual semantic masks across 257 object classes, 9.9M interpolated dense masks, and 67K hand–object relations using a semi-automated pipeline, and they release three benchmark challenges focusing on video object segmentation, interaction understanding, and long-term reasoning along with data, code, and leaderboards.

args.text: I propose Cross-Branch Guidance Linearization (CBGL) for diffusion transformers with classifier-free guidance: instead of executing both conditional and unconditional passes, we compute only the unconditional pass and synthesize the conditional layer outputs via a per-layer, low-rank affine map of the unconditional activation conditioned on the pooled text embedding, guidance scale, and timestep. A brief post-training calibration on a small prompt set learns these maps to minimize reconstruction error of the true conditional outputs, with a lightweight error monitor that occasionally triggers a real conditional pass to bound drift. CBGL generalizes CFG attention sharing by approximating the entire block output rather than just attention, and it composes with layer-caching/routers to further skip or extrapolate steps. Empirically, this should eliminate roughly one branch’s compute across many steps while preserving quality, yielding substantial end-to-end speedups in DiT-class models.

result.text: The paper addresses safe linear stochastic bandits where, at each round, the learner must satisfy an unknown linear baseline constraint—i.e., ensure instantaneous reward stays above a given lower bound—while still maximizing cumulative reward. The key insight is that stage-wise conservatism can be enforced with modest impact on learning by designing conservative variants of Thompson Sampling and UCB that maintain confidence-aware safety while preserving near-optimal regret. Concretely, the authors propose SCLTS and SCLUCB algorithms that use linear model estimates and safety-aware action selection rules to ensure the baseline constraint with high probability, achieving regret bounds O(√T log^{3/2}T) and O(√T log T) respectively, and they show these methods extend with simple modifications to bandit-feedback constraints, unknown baseline actions, and upper-bound safety constraints while significantly reducing the number of baseline plays compared to prior work.

result.text: The paper addresses the approximation gap between random-feature-based attention (RFA) and exact softmax attention in efficient transformer architectures. Its key insight is that RFA can be interpreted as a sum of control-variate estimators—one per sequence element—so that softmax attention can be seen as recoverable by appropriately manipulating these control variates, enabling variance reduction. Building on this view, the authors propose a flexible, learnable control-variate form that yields a novel attention mechanism with substantially reduced approximation error while preserving RFA’s linear time and space complexity, and they validate its effectiveness across vision and language benchmarks.
